items.Sentence: Fine Screening: Secondary treated wastewater from OCSD’s Reclamation Plant No. 1 is strained, or passed through rotating band fine-mesh screens
Fine Screening: ... and chlorinated (as needed) prior to microfiltration.

Microfiltration: Screened secondary effluent flows via gravity to 26 in-basin microfiltration (MF) cells containing submerged racks of hollow fiber membranes with a maximum pore size of 0.2 micron. Sodium hypochlorite is added as-needed to the MF feed to form a low level (3-5 mg/L) of chloramine
Screenings are dewatered and returned to OCSD for disposal.
c. Reverse Osmosis. The RO process will be bypassed when AWPF effluent is discharged to the Santa Ana River.
The advanced oxidation/disinfection process (AOP) consists of two steps: hydrogen peroxide addition and ultraviolet (UV) light treatment.
For direct discharge to the SAR, only UV treatment will be used.
Decarbonation and Lime Stabilization Process: This treatment process will be bypassed when AWPF effluent is discharged to the Santa Ana River.

Dechlorination and pH adjustment: After UV disinfection and prior to discharge to the Santa Ana River, the effluent stream may still contain some chloramines. Sodium bisulfate will be added for dechlorination, if needed.
